questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The language and the culture - I wanted to be able to speak the language so I only had to juggle the culture differences and the studies. 
Plus I had only heard fantastistic things about Canada. 

I initially wanted to go to the US, but ended up not putting the US on my list because of politics and elections.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is always a bit of administrative work, which can be quite a hurdle when you get there.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
We had an orientation made by students which was nice, along with a short orientation by the administrative staff which was nice. 
It was a little tricky because the campus/uni had barely opened after vacation when I got there.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had several orientations that you could choose to go to.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: A little confusing since the uni wasn't quite upon.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
We had to apply for housing - appartments with or without kitchens. 
I had to apply and pay some money to apply, because they weren't sure that there was enough housing.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
Both apartments with or without kitchens. 
Meal plans are mandatory if you dont have a kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to check up on the rules for meal
plan.There
are rules regarding what you can and cannot buy is (and it seems to differ depending on the store) and there is a spending limit for each purpose and also regarding what items you can buy, which is counterintuitive, since it is your own money.
The school will also keep the money if you don't spend them, so they make it possible to downgrade.
There is also a welfare check at one point, to check the state of your room, but that is easy to pass.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
We had to make sure that there was no overlap between what we choose and they changed professor when we had to start our courses. 

You register through a website similar to the CPH website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could contact the school and advisors, and they were very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I wanted, but they have a great concept where they make it possible for the students to change their courses the first 2 weeks in case you figure out that they classes really isn't for you.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Take the courses that are different and that seem exciting to you. 
It is all a new experience and you might as well take what you want. I also choose some classes that were comparable to the danish courses. 

Make sure to check where your exams lie and don't make a schedule that is overly exhausting for yourself. 
I had classes from 2:30-8:30pm each Tuesday and thursday and a class on Wednesday from 6:30-8:30 pm and I had 4 exams in 8-9 days, and while it worked out - I could definitely have planned it better.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I could only take BA courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It is very much a kind of lecture for some professors and some where late and left an hour early. 
Others were very engaging and recounted how they use their knowledge in real lift, which made it super interesting and exciting. 
One course that was different was about AI and that was very much a course based on discussion because there is almost no regulation, which was a nice break from "normal" law studies.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Patents, Evidence, Forensic Science, Emerging Tech: Law, policy & governance.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Evidence with Goddard and walker - even though it was late at night they were incredible engaging and they made they subject very understandable and made overviews for the students with the general rules and the exceptions - They made the course known for being notoriously tricky into a very interesting course. 

Forensic science - they invited all kind of experts like the ones you see on television i.e. Ballistics, fingerprints, DNA, handwriting and forensic scientist.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The food was quite expensive because it was mandatory for me to have a meal plan.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Books weren't as expensive as I only had to get one book. 

However I spent a lot on personal spending because it is cheaper to shop there for some stuff.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
They had a lot of clubs, from film to crochet, gaming, dancing and training - there was a lot for everyone. 
Be aware that this can clash with course schedule, which mine did so I unfortunately couldn't try the clubs except the gym.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Maybe try the gaming if you want new friends or crochet if you're creative.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Downtown and all the different culture"towns" - Chinatown, Koreatown, litte Greece and Italy 

We travelled to Montreal which I also recommend, as well as a maple syrup farm.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
The culture was easy and people are extremely friendly and helpful, but you might get more international friends than Canadian friends. 

Also the time difference and having to act in a diffenrent language 24/7 is hard, so there might be a need for some time to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open to the people and try to reach out first.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Their politeness is on a different level, so there is a lot of small talk, which isn't challenging, but you have to get used to it, when you come from a culture where people don't say hi or talk to strangers on the street. 

Also the way you address profs etc. is more formal than in Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved the small talk and the curiousity, friendliness and helpfullness of the Canadians.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Consider if you wanna live on campus i.e. because of meal plan. 

For public transport, depending on where you live, consider their Presto card. 

Engage in the orientations and the activities made by the students, They are very sweet and helpful.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
All of my new friends. You have a special connection because it is a very different experience, that is hard to explain to people who have not been on exchange, and you are very intensely together for 4-5 months. 

And new knowledge of a different legal system to which I can compare and discuss the danish system.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first couple of weeks because of the time difference, the new environment and having to figure out a lot of different stuff in another language.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
